Radial-velocity dataset seed38_diff4.

- 74 observations over a baseline of 211.9 days
- median reported uncertainty: 2.35 m/s
- instruments: instA
- host star mass: 0.85 solar masses
- submission attempts available: 5

Recover the planetary system that produced this signal: the number of
planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Initial hypothesis: start with a 1-planet model at **73.07 d**.

Why:
- It is by far the dominant peak (power 0.723, FAP ~ 0).
- It is well below the 211.9 d baseline, so it is constrained.
- The spectral window has no strong feature near 73 d, so this is unlikely to be cadence-driven.
- The next notable peak at **37.84 d** is very close to the **half-period harmonic/alias** of the 73 d signal:
  - half of 73.07 d = 36.53 d
  - double of 37.84 d = 75.68 d
  So I would not promote 37.84 d to a second planet yet; it is more plausibly a harmonic/alias of the main signal until residuals prove otherwise.
- The shorter-period peaks near 0.63–1.08 d sit close to daily-window structure and have poor FAPs, so they are not good planet candidates at this stage.

Please fit a **single Keplerian near 73.07 d** first, then inspect residuals. If the engineer finds the model incomplete, I want the residual periodogram checked before adding any second planet, with **37.84 d** the first alternate candidate to test only if it survives subtraction of the 73 d signal.

HANDOFF: engineer
